round1_to_round2.summary: All five agents took the round-1 fact corrections, and I checked each against the filings. The fair-value spread narrowed from $23.5-27.0 (mean $25.3) to $24.4-26.6 (mean $25.5). The 12-month ladder mean rose by about 0.01-0.015 at K = 21-31, and the 12-month cross-agent SD fell modestly (0.039 to 0.037 at K = 21, 0.017 to 0.012 at K = 31). The 1-month ladders converged much more: the SD at K = 26.18 fell from 0.016 to 0.003.
round1_to_round2.convergence_assessment: The 12-month convergence is mostly independent agreement on corrected facts, not anchoring. Each agent rebuilt its own EBITDA from guided volumes, giving 2027E of $1.45-1.75B on its own deck, and all five kept a fair value below my round-1 $27 and said why: a metals-deck haircut, volume execution, and Copper World capex. Agents 1 and 2 moved down, away from me, and 3, 4 and 5 moved up. Agent_2's 12-month ladder ended further from my round-1 ladder (mean abs gap 0.029 to 0.034). The 1-month convergence is mostly anchoring on my round-1 framing. All five adopted my unverified '~65%' in-window probability for Q3, the median of $26.3-26.4 tilted by the thin Oct-2 intraday print, and a sigma of 17.5-19%. Most of that is now one source counted five times. Agent_3's 1-month ladder matches agent_1's round-1 ladder to three decimals, but it is just lognormal(26.35, 0.175), as agent_3 states. It is the same parameters, not copying.

disagreements.topic: Fair value level after the corrections (r2 range $24.4-26.6 vs my r1 $27)
disagreements.positions: agent_1 $26.6, agent_3 $26.0, agent_4 $25.6, agent_2 $25.0, agent_5 $24.4. All five are below my round-1 $27, citing metals-deck haircuts (Cu $5.6-5.75, Au realized $3,750-3,900), a volume haircut to 150-155kt, and Copper World capex inflation.
disagreements.resolution: I moved my fair value to $26. The agents' decks are close to the company's own 2027 assumption ($5.80 Cu, $4,200 Au, Sep 28 6-K), so they are not unreasonable. Rebuilding from verified H1 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $743M (at roughly $5.9 Cu and $4,600 Au) gives about $1.5-1.6B for 2027: +30kt of copper adds about $0.2B, while gold about $600/oz lower on flat ounces (2027 guide 213-269koz vs 217-272koz) and copper about $0.25 lower take off about $0.2B. So $1.6B was the top of the reasonable range, not the middle. Consolidated EV/EBITDA (7x $1.55B = $24.4) and P/E ($1.6 x 15 = $24) sit below the SOTP ($27-28), and I blend these to about $26. The remaining gap to agents 5 and 2 is a deck choice, not a fact.
disagreements.evidence: Q2 2026 MD&A (H1 adjusted EBITDA $743.1M); 6-K 2026-03-27 3-year outlook (2027 gold 213-269koz, copper 140-184kt); 6-K 2026-09-28 footnote (company 2027 deck $5.80 / $4,200).

summary: In round 2 all five forecasters applied the filing-backed corrections. Fair values now cluster at $24.4-26.6 (mean $25.5), all below my round-1 $27, because each uses a haircut metals deck and an execution-haircut volume. That is independent agreement, since they moved in both directions from their round-1 numbers. The 1-month agreement, though, is my round-1 framing repeated five times. The new facts the agents introduced check out against the filings: the company's own 2027 deck of $5.80 / $4,200, H1 EBITDA of $743M, H1 copper of 56.2kt, BC Q2 costs of $3.22/lb, the 2022 dismissal of the federal suits, the contingent Section 232 tariff, and the Fujimori government. I trimmed my fair value to $26 and slightly fattened the 12-month left tail; otherwise the mean stands. P(>=$26) is about 52%, and the thesis breaks at $16.

Event risk is concentrated in the next three months (Q3 print, Copper World capex, Section 232 decision), so a small capped position is enough for diversifying commodity exposure in a cash-heavy portfolio.
